1. Nature. 1995 May 11;375(6527):121-3. doi: 10.1038/375121a0.

Are we aware of neural activity in primary visual cortex?

Crick F(1), Koch C.

Author information:
(1)Salk Institute, La Jolla, California 92037, USA.

Comment in
    Nature. 1995 Sep 28;377(6547):293-5. doi: 10.1038/377293b0.
    Nature. 1995 May 11;375(6527):106-7. doi: 10.1038/375106a0.

It is usually assumed that people are visually aware of at least some of the 
neuronal activity in the primary visual area, V1, of the neocortex. But the 
neuroanatomy of the macaque monkey suggests that, although primates may be aware 
of neural activity in other visual cortical areas, they are not directly aware 
of that in area V1. There is some psychophysical evidence in humans that 
supports this hypothesis.
